gate: R3 — does a rollout search pick a different move than MAG
verdict: R3 PASSES — divergence 80.2% against a self-disagreement floor of 31.4% on 121 decisions. These are different players, so an SPRT (R4) can tell them apart. A precondition for winning more, not evidence of it.

noise_floor.what: The SAME search, same candidates, same opponent policy, same everything it can see — only the seed differs. The truth there is 0.00 by construction, so whatever it reports is what the instrument invents.
noise_floor.reading: Divergence exceeds the floor by 48.8 points.

disagreement_gap_note: When they disagree, the search's pair is worth this much more BY ITS OWN LEAF. Not evidence it is better — only that the two rank the same menu differently. R4 answers "better".
caveats: Both players rank the SAME candidate set, so this is a disagreement about value and not about the menu.
The opponent is not modelled: it plays chooseAction during the stepped turn, identically for every candidate. This is a best response to a fixed opponent, not an equilibrium.
SWITCH CANDIDATES ARE ON THE MENU and are counted in `switches` above. They were excluded before commit b4ec80b, and the caveat that said so outlived the code by a day.
DIVERGENCE IS NOT SUCCESS. This measures whether the two are different players. Whether the different one is better is R4, and only an SPRT answers that.
